ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 Revision, effective 1 January 2025); Measures for Beneficial Owner Information Management (People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024); Measures for Financial Institutions' Anti-Money Laundering Customer Due Diligence and Beneficial Owner Identification (PBOC Order No. 1 [2017]); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China and its Implementing Regulations; PRC Company Law (2023 Revision).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) local Administration for Market Regulation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: EITHER (Hague Apostille Convention State): notarize at a PRC notary public, then obtain an apostille from the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs; OR (non-member State): notarize at a PRC notary public, authenticate through the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then complete consular legalization at the embassy or consulate of the destination jurisdiction. The two routes are parallel alternatives and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certified Corporate Status Record
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SAMR / National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: EITHER (Hague Apostille Convention State): notarize the certified record at a PRC notary public, then obtain an apostille from the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs; OR (non-member State): notarize, authenticate through the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the destination consulate or embassy. These routes are mutually exclusive and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the non-PRC investor, and legal counsel for the WFOE, with notarization of signatory capacity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: EITHER (Hague Apostille Convention State): notarize the signatures at a competent notary in the document's country of origin, then obtain an apostille from the originating state's competent authority; OR (non-member State): notarize the signatures, complete authentication at the originating Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and then obtain consular legalization at the destination state's embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive parallel paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and Articles of Association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders of the WFOE and registered PRC legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: EITHER (Hague Apostille Convention State): notarize the executed constitutional documents at a PRC notary public, then apply to the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs for an apostille; OR (non-member State): notarize at a PRC notary public, authenticate through the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then complete consular legalization at the destination state's embassy or consulate. Never execute both routes in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter / Bank Confirmation of Account and Signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing licensed bank in the investor's home jurisdiction or a licensed PRC branch
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: EITHER (Hague Apostille Convention State): notarize the bank officer's signature and bank capacity, then obtain an apostille from the competent authority in the issuing jurisdiction; OR (non-member State): notarize the bank officer's signature, authenticate through the issuing jurisdiction's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and then obtain consular legalization at the destination embassy or consulate. The two authentication routes are alternatives and must not be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, signatories, and senior managers of the WFOE must undergo enhanced due diligence before formation. Screening must cover the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the U.S. OFAC SDN and non-SDN sectoral sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions databases, PRC MOFCOM and PBOC asset-freeze and sanctions notices, Interpol red notices, domestic court enforcement and bankruptcy records, and adverse media. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) trigger enhanced monitoring, independent senior management approval, source of wealth and source of funds verification, and quarterly re-screening. Any hit on a sanctions or terrorism list requires immediate suspension of formation, a risk assessment, and where applicable a Suspicious Transaction Report to the China Financial Intelligence Unit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Independent Declaration and Reservation System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory enterprise name must be expressed in Simplified Chinese characters using the four-tier naming formula: [Administrative Division] + [Distinctive Trade Name] + [Industry or Business Characteristic] + [Organizational Form]. For a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise, the foreign investor's name may be transliterated phonetically into Chinese as the distinctive trade name; any English name is supplementary only and does not replace the Chinese legal name. Latin letters, Arabic numerals, and non-standard symbols are generally prohibited unless specifically approved, and the name must not resemble an existing registered name in the same trade or administrative area.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon final name rejection, counsel shall within 60 days file a written administrative reconsideration application with the immediately superior Administration for Market Regulation. The application must annex the refusal notice, the proposed name, evidence of unavailability, examples of previously approved comparable names, and legal argument on distinguishability. If administrative reconsideration fails, the applicant may initiate administrative litigation in the competent People's Court within six months, or re-file a revised name after curing the stated defect. Any extension request must be submitted before the 30-day reservation expires and requires a notarized board resolution or power of attorney.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable for a WFOE in the ISIC 6311 sector. PRC company law and WFOE implementing rules require the registered address to be the principal place of business, evidenced by a lawful lease or ownership certificate. The tax authority and a licensed RMB bank will reject a virtual-only address for the video chat social app industry because the business requires physical presence, labor contracts, social insurance records, servers, and operational logs. Even where a free trade zone permits concentrated or collective registration, the bank will still demand on-site operating evidence before opening a basic deposit account; therefore a virtual office is practically rejected for this medium-risk fintech-facing model.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) registered address matches the lease or ownership title; (2) company nameplate at the registered address; (3) physical staff presence and labor contracts; (4) social insurance and individual income tax filings; (5) computer equipment, servers, and application software logs; (6) accounting books, invoices, and bank statements; (7) compatibility of actual operations with the declared business scope. Quantified risk: approximately 75-90% for an app-based WFOE using any virtual office or mailing address within the first 12 months; approximately 20-30% where a fully staffed physical office exists with documentary and operational substance aligned to the registered address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan (R.O.C.) Company Act, Articles 6, 16, 17, 129, 156, 161, 172, 192, 216 and 387; Foreign Investment Act, Articles 4 through 7; Act Governing Relations between the People of Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area, Article 73; Regulations for the Permission of Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Areas.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA-DCA), Taiwan (R.O.C.), with prior investment approval from the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration of a Company Limited by Shares, with the Articles of Incorporation annexed and all supporting corporate and investment permission documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Taiwan Company Act; no minimum paid-in capital is prescribed and no blocked escrow account is required. However, any cash-credited paid-in capital must be actually remitted into a Taiwan bank account before the MOEA filing, and the filing must include a certified public accountant capital verification report, foreign exchange settlement certificate, and, for Mainland-area investors, the Investment Commission approval letter. The Articles may state a lower or zero initial paid-in capital if permitted by the Investment Commission.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS, the Company has been formed as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise in Taiwan under the Taiwan (R.O.C.) Company Act; and WHEREAS, the subscribers have subscribed for the shares set out in the Articles of Incorporation and desire to complete the statutory formation and authorization of banking and corporate governance matters; and WHEREAS, the applicability of the Foreign Investment Act and, where applicable, the Act Governing Relations between the People of Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area has been reviewed and the necessary investment permission has been submitted. NOW, THEREFORE, be it RESOLVED, as follows: 1. RESOLVED: Subject to final regulatory approval, the authorized share capital of the Company is [amount] New Taiwan Dollars, divided into [number] ordinary shares, and that the subscribers listed in the subscription schedule hereby subscribe for, take, and pay for the shares as set forth in the capital subscription statement, without prejudice to the fact that Taiwan law does not impose a minimum paid-up capital or an escrow holding period. 2. RESOLVED: The registered office of the Company shall be situated at [address], Taipei, Taiwan, and the Chairman and General Manager are authorized to execute a lease, file the address with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, and notify the National Taxation Bureau; the Company shall maintain at that address the statutory books, seal, and corporate records. 3. RESOLVED: The Company shall open operating account or accounts with [Bank], [Branch], and shall deposit all paid-in capital funds and operational receipts with such bank. Each of [Director A] and [General Manager B] is authorized severally to execute all account-opening agreements, mandates, and instruments; provided, however, that any outward payment exceeding USD [amount] shall require two signatures, one of whom must be the Chairman. 4. RESOLVED: [Director A] is hereby appointed as Chairman, [General Manager B] as General Manager, and [Supervisor C] as Supervisor, each to hold office in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation and to exercise the powers approved by the Board; the Chairman and General Manager are jointly authorized to file the incorporation application with the Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, to execute all forms, to pay registration fees, and to complete any post-registration filings concerning labor insurance, health insurance, and taxation. 5. RESOLVED: Any one of the Chairman, General Manager, or the corporate secretary designated by them may apply for certified copies of company registry records, appear before notary and government authorities, and take all necessary steps to render this resolution effective and to carry out the incorporation. All actions previously taken by the promoters and officers with respect to the foregoing matters are hereby ratified and approved, and this resolution shall be effective as of [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Obtain Foreign and Mainland-Area Investment Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: One-Stop Company Name Pre-Application Online System, Ministry of Economic Affairs; Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign or Mainland-area corporate shareholder must submit an investment license application to the Investment Commission before the incorporation registration. For a Mainland-area parent, cross-strait company documents must be notarized in China and authenticated by the Straits Exchange Foundation in Taipei. The application includes a business plan, qualified shareholder structure, proposed paid-in capital, and the proposed company name reserved online in accordance with Article 16 of the Taiwan Company Act. The company name and business scope are checked for conflict with registered trademarks and prohibited undertakings. The Investment Commission will review the applicant identity, funding sources, and permissible business scope and, upon approval, will issue a foreign investment approval letter or a mainland investment permission order.
required_dossiers: Notarized and authenticated parent company board resolution and power of attorney
Application Form for Investment by Mainland-Area Person or Company
Audited financial statements of the direct shareholder for the preceding year
Business plan including capital injection timeline and source of funds
Certificate of company name reservation and proposed Articles of Incorporation
Identity documents of directors, supervisor, and ultimate beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a correction letter or suspends the application, counsel must file a response through the same online portal within 14 calendar days addressing the requested documentary gaps; a materially adverse decision may be appealed to the Executive Yuan under the administrative appeal procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Foreign Exchange Trust Account and Remit Paid-In Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized banking institutions designated by the Central Bank of China (Taiwan)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once investment approval is received, the company remits the approved foreign capital to a temporary New Taiwan Dollar account at a designated bank in Taiwan, opened in the name of the company under formation. The remitting bank issues a foreign exchange settlement certificate and a certified remittance notice. Taiwan Company Act does not prescribe a minimum capital or blocked escrow account; nevertheless, capital contributed in cash must actually be received before registration. The corporate attorney must instruct a Taiwan certified public accountant to issue a capital verification report covering the paid-in capital, period of payment, and bank statements. If the proposed business is purely digital and no paid-in capital is initially subscribed, a declaration of zero paid-in capital may be filed, subject to the Articles of Incorporation and Investment Commission conditions.
required_dossiers: Foreign or mainland investment approval letter
Proposed Articles of Incorporation
Company name reservation notice
Applicant identification documents and board resolution appointing subscriber
Bank remittance application and power of attorney to the foreign exchange bank
Draft paid-in capital schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If remittance is blocked by the central bank or the receiving bank, the investor should apply to the Investment Commission for a revised inward remittance classification and provide a letter of undertaking from a Taiwan-designated bank; bank refusal due to AML or CFT causes must be cured by submitting updated ultimate beneficial ownership declarations and transaction chain evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene Incorporation Meeting and Adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Promoters and initial subscribers, assisted by a Taiwan certified public accountant or corporate attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The sole shareholder or the initial subscribers must convene an incorporation meeting in Taiwan or adopt a written resolution to ratify the Articles, subscribe shares, approve the first board of directors, and appoint a supervisor. The first board then adopts the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution included in this dossier, approving share subscription, banking authorization, registered office adoption, and statutory officer appointments. All minutes must be signed by the chairperson and secretary and must be retained with the statutory corporate records. For a privately held Taiwan company limited by shares, the minutes do not require court or notarial approval; however, all signatures on the incorporation minutes should be affixed under civil identity legal responsibility and may be notarized if requested by the bank or the Ministry of Economic Affairs examiner.
required_dossiers: Incorporation meeting minutes
First board resolution adopted in accordance with the Pro-Forma text
Consent letters of directors and supervisor
Statement of capital subscription
Statement of registered office address and lease consent
Acceptance letters of statutory officer appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any statutory officer withdraws consent before filing, the remaining shareholders should sign additional consent forms and, where required, convene a new general meeting; any omission in the minutes should be corrected by a supplemental resolution dated before the MOEA filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (Company Registration Online System)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporation application must be submitted to the Department of Commercial Affairs, MOEA, through the Company Registration Online System or in person, together with the application form, Articles of Incorporation, incorporation minutes, first board resolution, capital verification report, officer consents, lease proof, and foreign or mainland investment approval. The examiner will verify the company name, business scope, capital structure, officer qualifications, and compliance with the Taiwan Company Act. If all documents are in order and the electronic stamp duty and registration fee have been paid, MOEA will issue the Company Registration Certificate and company registration number. Under Article 6 of the Taiwan Company Act, the company is deemed legally established upon completion of this registration, and the formation date will be recorded accordingly.
required_dossiers: Company incorporation application form
Articles of Incorporation in duplicate
Incorporation meeting minutes
First board resolution
Capital verification report by a Taiwan certified public accountant
Investment Commission approval letter
Registered office lease or ownership certificate with use consent
Consent letters of directors and supervisor
Photocopies of passports or identity documents of statutory officers
Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a correction order or rejects the filing, the applicant has 30 days to correct, re-file through the online portal with superseding documents, and respond to the examiner's query; if registration is refused on material legal grounds, seek administrative appeal to the Executive Yuan within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax Registration, Unified Business Number, and Post-Incorporation Government Notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance), Bureau of Labor Insurance (Ministry of Labor), National Health Insurance Administration (Ministry of Health and Welfare), and, if appropriate, Ministry of Digital Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After MOEA registration, the company must, within 15 days, register with the National Taxation Bureau to obtain the unified business number and business tax certificate, and, if it will issue invoices, file the invoice book application. Because the activity is a digital social-app platform, no environmental industrial permit, Civil Defense fire certificate, or manufacturing plant license is required. However, the company must register as an employer with the labor insurance and national health insurance authorities and establish a payroll and occupational accident notification procedure. The company should also verify with the Ministry of Digital Affairs whether the OTT or video-matching service triggers any telecommunication license; for a pure content platform, no Type II telecommunication license is generally required.
required_dossiers: MOEA company registration certificate
Unified business number application form
Registered office lease or ownership certificate
Bank account certificate and foreign exchange remittance record
List of directors and statutory officers
Declaration that no industrial or environmental operating permit is applicable
Tax registration or business registration application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the taxation bureau delays issuance of the unified business number, the applicant may file an appeal with the branch and, if no resolution occurs within 30 days, apply to the Ministry of Finance; any late-registration penalty should be mitigated by showing good faith, prompt filing, and the digital-only nature of the business.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial or manufacturing authority has jurisdiction over ISIC 6311 digital data processing and video-matching platform operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industry-specific operating or manufacturing permit is required for the registered digital social app business.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no physical project is subject to the Taiwan Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - pure digital service with no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing footprint.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero industrial wastewater, VOCs, or hazardous waste streams; ordinary commercial office operations must only comply with standard municipal waste and building code requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no warehouse, chemical, assembly, or manufacturing premises are occupied; the registered office must nonetheless maintain ordinary fire-safety compliance under the Taiwan Building Act and local Civil Defense evacuation rules.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online taxpayer portal: National Electronic Tax Bureau / electronic tax bureau at etax.chinatax.gov.cn, supplemented by the provincial electronic tax bureaus.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a mainland China Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) limited liability company, the TIN is the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) under the 'one license, one code' reform. The statute requires (1) foreign investor submits the foreign investment information registration through the SAMR platform; (2) upon issuance of the business license, the WFOE automatically obtains its unified social credit code, which serves as the enterprise TIN for enterprise income tax, VAT, and other national taxes; (3) the WFOE must complete supplementary tax registration, legal representative and financial officer identity filing, and bank account filing through the electronic tax bureau within 30 calendar days; (4) if annual taxable turnover is projected to exceed the VAT threshold or input credit is required, the WFOE must apply for general VAT taxpayer status through the same portal; and (5) the WFOE must enroll in the electronic invoice service platform for digital invoice issuance. A non-resident foreign entity without a Chinese establishment or place of business may obtain a TIN by direct non-resident enterprise tax registration or through a withholding agent, using legalized incorporation documents, charter, board resolution appointing a tax representative, and the relevant Chinese-sourced income contract; in such case the TIN is issued by the competent STA office and is distinct from the unified social credit code. This China WFOE does not obtain any Taiwanese tax identification number solely by reason of its PRC incorporation; a Taiwan tax ID would arise only upon separate branch/permanent establishment registration in Taiwan.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not maintain a check-the-box or pass-through election for a WFOE. Hybrid mismatch and controlled foreign corporation adjustments are handled through the statutory CFC rules, General Anti-Avoidance Rules, and special tax adjustment provisions of the Enterprise Income Tax Law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Provisional Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Value Added Tax and the Cai Shui [2016] 36 Circular implementing the conversion from business tax to VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable turnover (CNY 5 million) is the mandatory statutory threshold for registration as a general VAT taxpayer; below this threshold small-scale taxpayer treatment applies, but all business entities must complete tax registration regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China requires VAT invoices to be issued through the STA-controlled electronic invoice service platform under the fully digital electronic invoice system integrated with Golden Tax Phase IV. Invoice data is transmitted to the tax authority in real time via API in XML format with a unique anti-counterfeit QR code and digital signature. General VAT taxpayers must use online invoice verification and may not issue offline paper invoices except under approved special circumstances; abnormal issuance triggers automated risk control.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export treatment applies to goods physically exported from the customs territory of China and to qualifying offshore services supplied to non-resident customers and fully consumed outside China. For the ISIC 6311 video matching and cross-border social telephony app, zero-rating may be claimed for exported software/video/telephony services only where the recipient is an overseas entity or individual, the service is not used or consumed in China, payment is received in foreign exchange, and the service is consistently documented as a cross-border taxable service under the Cai Shui [2016] 36 Circular.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) for goods movements, with China customs release notation
Bill of Lading or equivalent air waybill evidencing export from the PRC
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank receipt of foreign currency export proceeds
Foreign exchange transaction declaration under the foreign exchange administration for goods or service trade
Commercial invoice and packing list issued by the exporter
Cross-border service contract or order evidencing the non-resident recipient and foreign exchange payment
Electronic VAT export invoice issued through the STA electronic invoice platform
Service trade foreign exchange tax filing/recordal where required by the tax authority
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Upon audit, if the export zero-rating claim is not substantiated, the STA will claw back the VAT refunded, impose late payment interest, and assess an additional penalty ranging from 50 percent to five times the tax involved depending on whether the defect is classified as underreporting or fraud. Criminal liability for fraudulent export VAT refunds is addressed under Article 204 of the Criminal Law, with imprisonment up to life and fines up to five times the defrauded amount. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day statutory period may also result in State Administration of Foreign Exchange penalties, forfeiture of input tax refunds, and credit blacklisting.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) with delegated foreign exchange administration authority conferred upon the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The PRC operates a managed conditional convertibility regime. The lawful foreign exchange market is restricted to designated banks, with SAFE and PBOC exercising comprehensive supervision. Current account transactions, including cross-border service fees, royalties, dividends, and ordinary trade proceeds, are generally convertible when the underlying transaction is genuine and documentation is submitted to a designated bank. Profit remittances from a WFOE to its Taiwan shareholder are treated as current account outflows but require annual audited financial statements, a tax clearance certificate proving that final corporate income tax has been settled, a board resolution declaring dividends, and a bank-level authenticity review. Inbound registered capital injections are capital account transactions and remain heavily controlled: the Taiwan investor must first complete SAFE foreign exchange registration and the WFOE must open a specially designated Foreign Currency Capital Account. Once received, capital can be settled into RMB for actual business purposes but may not be deployed into securities, real estate beyond the negative list, entrusted loans, or speculative derivatives. Export proceeds have no general compulsory surrender ratio; however, all foreign exchange receipts must be repatriated into the domestic banking system within the statutory period and cannot be retained offshore without prior SAFE approval. This asymmetry between current account convertibility and capital account prior-approval determines the entire treasury architecture and requires disciplined cross-border liquidity planning.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China no longer imposes a blanket mandatory conversion percentage for export proceeds. For standard A-class enterprises, the statutory rule is repatriation within 180 days from the customs export declaration date, or from the contractual payment date if the underlying trade terms are registered and reported in the Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring System; delayed collection must be declared and substantiated to SAFE. The mandatory conversion ratio is 0% for A-class enterprises, which may freely retain export receipts in a Foreign Currency Settlement Account or voluntarily convert them to RMB at market rates through a designated bank. B-class and C-class enterprises are subject to enhanced review and may be required by SAFE to settle 100% of export foreign exchange receipts into RMB within 90 days, alongside complete transaction documentation and more frequent compliance reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Currency Capital Account for SAFE-registered FDI capital injection

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Deposit Account and CNY operating treasury account
Foreign Currency Settlement Account for current account trade and service receipts
Cross-border RMB settlement account and service trade disbursement account
Operational RMB payroll and expense clearing account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary treasury rail for this mainland WFOE. Offshore fintech EMIs do not possess a designated foreign exchange bank licence issued by PBOC/SAFE, cannot independently complete SAFE foreign exchange registration, cannot clear CNY through CNAPS or CIPS, and are legally barred from directly opening corporate bank accounts for domestic entities. Their only permissible role is ancillary international collection, for example receiving settlement from Paymentwall or Apple IAP through a licensed mainland payment institution partner, provided that the partner obtains the necessary PBOC/SAFE cross-border payment authorisation and all funds ultimately flow into a Tier-1 domestic bank account with proper transaction coding. The WFOE should not rely on offshore EMIs for capital account flows, statutory tax remittances, dividend distributions, or FX hedging.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical in-branch appearance is required. The statutory legal representative, the local financial controller, and authorised signatories must attend a face-to-face AML KYC interview at the domestic branch of the Tier-1 bank. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted for the initial corporate account opening; online/video pre-screening may be possible, but original business registration papers, legal representative identification, company seal imprint verification, and hard-copy resolutions must be executed on site. The bank will also conduct a physical compliance site inspection of the registered office and cross-check the WFOE's tax and SAFE filing status before full activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layer opacity in ultimate beneficial ownership arising from a Taiwan holding company or family investment vehicle, making it difficult for the bank to identify all natural persons owning or controlling the WFOE.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership chain from each ultimate individual shareholder through every intermediate holding layer to the CN WFOE, evidenced by notarised and legalised certificates of incorporation, memoranda and articles of association, current registers of members, UBO declarations, passport copies, an ownership diagram, audited financial statements for the parent and any intermediate entities for at least 24 months, source-of-wealth records, bank reference letters, and tax residence certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume in-app user payments through Apple IAP and Paymentwall, creating a perceived risk of third-party money laundering, chargeback abuse, layering, and insufficient transaction visibility.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Identical merchant agreements with Apple and Paymentwall, a technical transaction-flow narrative showing how user payments convert into merchant settlements, end-user KYC documentation and age-verification protocols, sanctions screening screenshots, real-time transaction monitoring reports, chargeback and fraud management policies, PCI-DSS or SOC 2 reports, monthly settlement reconciliation statements, historical volume and velocity statistics, and the CV of the appointed AML compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-strait investment sensitivity: inbound equity capital from Taiwan may attract enhanced political and source-of-funds scrutiny, particularly if the bank cannot verify mainland investment approval and SAFE registration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Mainland foreign investment filing certificate or negative-list compliance statement, SAFE FDI foreign exchange registration certificate issued by the local branch, CPA-issued capital verification report prepared after the Taiwan shareholder remits funds, SWIFT confirmation from the remitting bank, annotated bank statements for the source account, a certified translation of Taiwanese corporate registration documents, shareholder loan/funding agreements, and corporate resolutions authorising the cross-border capital transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The stated business of real-time random video matching and cross-border social telephony may be interpreted by the underwriting committee as an adult-content-adjacent or high-risk user-generated-content platform vulnerable to criminal exploitation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A substantive compliance package containing internet content and network security filings, user terms and privacy policy that prohibit unlawful soliciting, nudity and financial fraud, robust content moderation workflows, automated image and text abuse detection, user reporting tools, no acceptance of anonymous cash deposits, a formal written certification that the platform is not adult-entertainment oriented, litigation and sanctions clean certificates, audited financial statements for the first operating period, and a written AML/CTF risk assessment prepared by an external consultant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan parent must complete SAFE foreign exchange registration for the WFOE and then remit equity capital from its Taiwan bank account via SWIFT into the dedicated Foreign Currency Capital Account opened at a Tier-1 domestic commercial bank such as Bank of China Limited. The remittance instruction must carry the SAFE foreign exchange business purpose code for inbound FDI capital injection, commonly reported as 126011, and must reference the SAFE FDI registration serial number. Upon receipt, the domestic bank verifies the sending institution, remitter name, purpose code, and underlying registration record. The WFOE then appoints a licensed PRC certified public accountant to issue the statutory capital verification report. The capital funds may later be converted into RMB under the SAFE capital account easy-settlement policy for genuine business purposes, subject to the negative list and explicit prohibition on use for securities, entrusted loans, speculative derivatives, or repayment of RMB loans before the capital contribution duties are satisfied.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For genuine outbound disbursements such as cloud service fees, software license royalties, overseas content moderation, marketing and contractor payments, the WFOE must submit a service trade foreign exchange payment application to its settlement bank, attaching the underlying commercial contract, original invoice, tax withholding/acquisition certificate, and transaction authenticity declaration. The bank executes the remittance through SWIFT MT103; multi-currency high-value payments may be routed through CIPS or the offshore clearing system while respecting SWIFT message format standards. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are available for physical equipment or infrastructure procurement and must be issued through the corporate bank with strict compliance checks over beneficiary names, shipping documents, bill of lading, insurance certificates, and sanctioned-country restrictions. All outbound payments must be benchmarked against fair market value to avoid transfer pricing and underground remittance red flags.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore CNY/USD, CNY/EUR and CNY/TWD forward contracts with genuine current-account or capital-account exposure; the WFOE must furnish underlying transaction documentation and forward contracts must be executed in the name of the WFOE itself, with no speculative or naked positions permitted.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for offshore borrowing or long-term FDI capital exposure, subject to SAFE registration, external debt or equity notional correspondence, and utilisation only through a qualified onshore designated bank.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible on a standalone onshore basis for the mainland WFOE because onshore hedging must be deliverable under SAFE rules; the Taiwan parent may execute NDFs offshore, but any resulting gain or loss cannot be booked as a synthetic onshore hedge absent a genuine intra-group netting structure approved by the bank and SAFE.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding income tax statement and annual income withholding forms covering salaries, director fees, dividends, royalties, and other Taiwan-sourced payments to residents and non-residents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance having jurisdiction over the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before January 31 following the close of the taxable year; non-resident payments are also subject to the 10-day post-payment filing rule with the annual consolidated statement due by January 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under Article 114 of the Income Tax Act, a withholding agent that fails to withhold or file the annual statement may be penalized one to one and one-half times the tax withheld; failure to issue withholding certificates may trigger fines of TWD 1,500 to TWD 7,500 per certificate; continued noncompliance may result in tax liens, enforced collection, and referral of the dormant entity for administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and payment, including related-party transaction disclosure and transfer pricing documentation when statutory thresholds are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance having jurisdiction over the company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 1 through May 31 following the close of the calendar fiscal year; a one-month extension to June 30 is available only upon approved application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a surcharge of 3% of unpaid tax for every two days of delay, capped at 10% of the unpaid tax; understated or omitted taxable income may be penalized by an additional one to two times the understated tax; failure to file after official summons leads to estimated assessment; a company that ceases business for six months or more may be administratively dissolved by the Ministry of Economic Affairs under Article 10 of the Company Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual regular shareholders' meeting approval of the business report, financial statements, and profit distribution or accumulated-loss compensation proposal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders in general meeting; the executed minutes must be retained at the registered office and made available to the Ministry of Economic Affairs and tax authorities for inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, no later than June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the regular shareholders' meeting within the statutory period exposes responsible directors to administrative fines of TWD 10,000 to TWD 50,000, with possible successive fines after a remedial deadline; prolonged failure together with cessation of business may be treated as abnormal operation and trigger administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign investment operation and performance report filed for the Taiwan WFOE's foreign shareholder
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the fiscal year, by June 30, or such earlier date as stated in the foreign investment approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may delay or block approval of dividend remittances, capital gain transfers, or repatriation of original invested capital; repeated or serious noncompliance may result in withdrawal or revocation of the foreign investment approval, forcing divestment, share transfer restrictions, or involuntary liquidation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A non-public Taiwan company must have its annual financial statements audited and certified by a licensed certified public accountant when it meets any one of the thresholds under Article 20 of the Company Act and related regulations: (1) paid-in capital of at least TWD 30 million; (2) operating revenue of at least TWD 100 million in the most recent fiscal year; or (3) more than 100 employees. Publicly issued companies are always subject to statutory CPA audit. In addition, the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs may require audited financial statements for foreign-invested companies even below the general thresholds, and the tax authority may require audited statements in an investigation or audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan-IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission for public companies and certain large non-public companies; non-public SME companies may apply the Enterprise Accounting Standard for SMEs; all statutory books must comply with the Business Entity Accounting Act, related regulations, and the Income Tax Act for tax accounting purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan's corporate transparency regime is event-driven rather than an open public annual UBO registry. The company must maintain an accurate shareholder register and beneficial-ownership records at its registered office and file any required change registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 15 days after a share transfer or other registrable ownership change. In the annual cycle, shareholders confirm current shareholding and ultimate beneficial ownership at the annual general meeting; for any transfer outside that cycle, the completed ownership event must be documented and the 30-day reporting window for final UBO confirmation must be strictly observed. Failure to update the statutory register within the applicable period makes the ownership change ineffective against third parties and exposes responsible officers to administrative fines.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 16,000 per audit cycle, higher if group-reporting, transfer-pricing documentation, or IFRS conversion is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% preferential rate for qualified High and New Technology Enterprises (HNTE); effective 5% tax rate for Small Low-Profit Enterprises with annual taxable income up to RMB 3 million, employees up to 300, and total assets up to RMB 50 million, and effective 10% for taxable income between RMB 3 million and RMB 5 million during 2023-2027; 100% additional deduction for qualifying R&D expenses (i.e., double deduction of eligible R&D costs); 'two-year exemption and three-year half rate' for qualified software enterprises; accelerated depreciation for specific equipment investments; certain regional free-trade-zone incentives may apply depending on the location of the WFOE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Type A) - Form A100000 (中华人民共和国企业所得税年度纳税申报表（A类）) filed electronically via the State Taxation Administration's e-Tax Bureau (电子税务局).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly provisional payments made within 15 days after each quarter-end; annual settlement by May 31 of the following year).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within 5 months of the fiscal year-end (i.e., no later than May 31). Quarterly provisional tax returns must be filed within 15 days after the end of each quarter (April 15, July 15, October 15, January 15).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Operating Revenue - gross receipts from video matching subscriptions, virtual gifts, advertising, and ancillary services attributable to the WFOE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize revenue pursuant to PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises. For sales through Apple IAP and Paymentwall, report gross revenue as principal after considering the commission and distribution structure; commissions are deducted as costs, not netted against revenue. Revenue from related parties (e.g., the Taiwan parent) must be at arm's length and supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation. VAT is excluded from this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of Sales - direct costs including cloud hosting, bandwidth, content moderation, payment processing fees, royalties, and other direct service costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments to non-residents (e.g., licensing software from the Taiwan parent) must be examined for withholding tax obligations. Deductibility is denied if the payment does not satisfy arm's length principles or if actual services/licence are not substantiated. If the WFOE pays royalties or service fees to the Taiwan parent, a 10% withholding tax is triggered on the gross payment (plus VAT on royalties), and the tax authority will scrutinize the commercial reality and valuation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and Surcharges - urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharges, property tax, stamp duty, and other deductible taxes (excluding VAT and corporate income tax).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax fines, late payment surcharges and criminal penalties are not deductible and must be added back in Box 8. Ensure all taxes and surcharges are correctly accrued in the year to which they relate; cross-border housing tax or property held by the WFOE is fully taxable on the PRC entity with no non-resident relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Period Expenses - selling, general and administrative expenses: salaries, rent, marketing, legal and accounting fees, depreciation of office equipment and IT infrastructure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid to the Taiwan parent are deductible only where the parent performs genuine services with verifiable evidence (service agreements, invoices, time records, and economic substance). Payments that represent disguised profit distribution or shareholder costs will be disallowed and treated as a deemed dividend, attracting a 10% withholding tax. Strictly maintain transfer pricing documentation for all intercompany service fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating Profit - the net result from principal operations calculated as Box 1 less Box 2 less Box 3 less Box 4.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a tax authority transfer pricing adjustment is made to increase revenue or reduce costs, the adjusted operating profit must be reconciled in Box 8. The WFOE must ensure that its reported profit is consistent with the arm's length standard for cross-border transactions with the Taiwan parent and other related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-Operating Income and Expenses - gains or losses on disposal of fixed assets, donations, penalties and fines, litigation settlements, and foreign exchange gains or losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fines, penalties, and late payment surcharges imposed by tax or other authorities are non-deductible and must be separately added back in Box 8. Donations are deductible only to the extent provided by law and made through qualified public welfare organizations; otherwise they must be added back. Realized exchange differences from cross-border transactions are recognized under PRC GAAP and are generally taxable or deductible, subject to verification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Profit - algebraic sum of operating profit (Box 5) and non-operating income/expenses (Box 6).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the starting point for tax reconciliation. Verify consistency with the audited financial statements. For a WFOE, all worldwide income of the resident enterprise is subject to PRC corporate income tax; however, any income attributable to a Taiwan permanent establishment may be eligible for foreign tax credit as described in Box 15.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Adjustment Increases - all non-deductible expenses, unreported revenue, transfer pricing upward adjustments, and disallowed depreciation or amortization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include any excessive intercompany interest where the Taiwan parent's loan is thinly capitalized beyond the debt-equity ratio (2:1 for financial institutions, 2:1 for others) under Article 46 of the EIT Law. Transfer pricing adjustments proposed during an audit must be reflected here, adding to taxable income. Undocumented or unsupported cross-border management fees also belong here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Adjustment Decreases - deductions that were not recognized in accounting profit but are allowed for tax purposes, such as accelerated depreciation, amortization of intangible assets at different rates, and other reconciling items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The most significant decrease is the 100% additional deduction for qualifying R&D expenses incurred by the WFOE in developing its video-matching algorithm and related software. This effectively reduces taxable income by an amount equal to 100% of eligible R&D costs (i.e., double deduction). Maintain complete R&D project files, personnel lists, and cost allocations to support the claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt Income and Reduced-Income Items - tax-exempt income such as qualified government bond interest, transferred-in income, and certain derisked income; also includes additional deductions under incentive regimes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the typical WFOE, most operating income is taxable; no blanket exemption exists for foreign-source income, as China taxes its resident enterprises on worldwide income. Certain software enterprises may claim the 'two-year exemption, three-year half rate' incentive in this line. Non-resident shareholders derive no benefit from this line; its purpose is to reduce the WFOE's own taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable Income - total profit (Box 7) adjusted by Box 8, Box 9, and Box 10, after applying loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Net operating losses may be carried forward for 5 years (10 years for qualified high-tech enterprises and technology-oriented SMEs, if conditions are met). Losses of a foreign branch are generally not allowed to reduce PRC taxable income unless certain recapture rules apply. The WFOE should calculate this line after considering the loss carryforward before adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable Tax Rate - 25% standard rate; 15% for HNTE; 20% for Small Low-Profit Enterprises (with effective 5%/10% preferential rates applied via Line 14).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE should evaluate eligibility for HNTE status, as its artificial-intelligence and video-matching software development activities may satisfy the R&D intensity and core intellectual property ownership tests. A valid HNTE certificate must be secured before filing; otherwise the 25% rate applies. The 15% rate is inserted here; any residual benefit is further reflected in Line 14.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income Tax Payable - taxable income (Box 11) multiplied by the applicable rate in Box 12.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the preliminary corporate income tax before any reductions or credits. For income derived from Taiwan (e.g., licensing revenue from a Taiwanese customer or a Taiwan branch), the related foreign tax credit is computed in Line 15, not here. Any special tax adjustment interest from transfer pricing audits is not included in this line; it is reported separately as interest surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Reductions and Exemptions - preferential reductions for qualified software enterprises, integrated circuit enterprises, and other statutory incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE that qualifies as a software enterprise may claim the 'two-year exemption, three-year half rate' incentive; if it is also an HNTE, coordination of the two regimes is required to avoid double-dipping. The amount of reduction is entered here. If the WFOE is a small low-profit enterprise, the effective reduction from 25% to 5% or 10% is also reflected here via a supplementary schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Credit - foreign tax credits for income taxes paid outside China and credits for qualifying purchases of special equipment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE pays Taiwan income tax on income sourced from Taiwan (e.g., profits from a Taiwanese PE or Taiwanese-source royalty income), it may claim a foreign tax credit equal to the lesser of the foreign tax paid and the PRC tax attributable to that foreign-source income. Submit Taiwan tax payment certificates, tax computation schedules, and a claim under Article 23 of the EIT Law. No treaty is currently in force with Taiwan, so the credit is based solely on the domestic law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Actual Income Tax Payable - Box 13 minus Box 14 minus Box 15.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the final net corporate income tax liability before considering quarterly prepayments. Ensure that the aggregate of all tax incentives and credits does not exceed the preliminary tax. The WFOE should verify its effective tax rate is consistent with its incentive certificates and prior year assessments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepaid Income Tax - total provisional corporate income tax payments already made quarterly during the current year, plus any tax withheld at source on behalf of the WFOE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quarterly prepayments are due within 15 days after each quarter-end. If the WFOE underestimated its quarterly payments, an interest surcharge is applicable on the underpayment until settlement; the annual return due May 31 will reconcile the balance. Keep all payment vouchers and bank receipts for filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance Due or Refund - actual income tax payable (Box 16) less prepaid income tax (Box 17).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any remaining balance is due by May 31 following the fiscal year-end. If a refund is due, the WFOE may claim it through the e-Tax Bureau; refunds are subject to tax authority review. This line does not relate to dividend withholding tax: the 10% withholding on distributions to the Taiwan parent is filed separately under the withholding return and is not included in this corporate tax return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: a fine of up to RMB 2,000 for ordinary cases and RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 for serious cases, plus a late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on unpaid tax (TCAL Article 32). Failure to file quarterly provisional returns incurs similar fines. Incorrect or fraudulent filing leading to underpayment of tax constitutes tax evasion under TCAL Article 63, subject to 50%-500% penalty on the evaded tax and criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 201. Non-submission of transfer pricing documentation may trigger a penalty under TCAL Article 62 and enable the tax authority to estimate income using reasonable methods, adding interest at benchmark rate plus 5 percentage points. The WFOE will also be listed in the Major Tax Violation Case List, resulting in joint disciplinary measures including travel bans and market access restrictions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% - dividends distributed by the PRC WFOE to its Taiwan non-resident enterprise shareholder are subject to a statutory withholding tax of 10% under Articles 3 and 37 of the EIT Law. There is no effective cross-strait tax treaty to reduce this rate; therefore, the 10% rate applies on the gross dividend amount. The WFOE, as the withholding agent, must deduct and remit the tax to the State Taxation Administration within 7 days of the date of payment (or designating the dividend in accordance with law).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No treaty relief is currently available between the PRC and Taiwan because the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement signed in 2015 has not yet entered into force. If the agreement becomes effective, the WFOE (or the Taiwan shareholder) would need to: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Taiwan tax authority in the prescribed form; (2) complete and submit the Beneficial Ownership Self-Certification, proving that the Taiwan recipient is the beneficial owner of the dividends and has not been interposed for treaty shopping purposes; (3) submit the TRC and certificate to the PRC withholding tax authority before the dividend payment is made or within the statutory time for the withholding filing; (4) obtain a written confirmation or approval from the tax authority to apply the treaty-reduced rate (typically 5% under the draft agreement); and (5) maintain supporting documents for a minimum of 10 years. Until the agreement is activated, the WFOE must apply the full 10% statutory withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT rate for interest paid to a non-resident enterprise is 10% on the gross amount (EIT Law Article 37); statutory WHT rate for royalties is also 10% on the gross amount. No treaty rate applies to Taiwan residents because no DTA is in force. For royalty payments, in addition to the 10% income tax, Chinese VAT at 6% (plus local surcharges on VAT) is required to be withheld by the WFOE, bringing the total effective tax burden on royalties to approximately 16.97% (10% income tax + 6% VAT plus surcharges on the VAT). For interest, the lender may also be subject to VAT at 6% on a gross-basis withholding, with the same surcharges; however, certain interbank financial interest may be exempt if the lender meets specific conditions. If the WFOE has a permanent establishment in China to which the interest or royalty is effectively connected, the income is taxed on a net basis at the standard corporate rate instead of the 10% WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File preparation thresholds under SAT Announcement 2016 No. 42: annual related-party tangible asset transfers exceeding RMB 200 million; financial asset transfers exceeding RMB 100 million; intangible asset transfers exceeding RMB 100 million; or other related-party transactions (including service fees, interest, and other flows) exceeding RMB 40 million. Master File preparation is required when aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion. Even below these thresholds, the WFOE must file the annual related-party transaction reporting schedules with the corporate income tax return, and the tax authority may require a Local File in a targeted risk assessment.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The PRC does not have a dedicated Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime akin to offshore financial centers, but substantive economic presence is required under the general anti-abuse rule (GAAR) in EIT Law Article 47, the controlled foreign corporation (CFC) rules in Article 45, and the substance-over-form principle in tax collection. The WFOE must be able to demonstrate that it performs core income-generating activities (CIGA) in China, including software development, server hosting, data processing, customer support, and strategic decision-making. If the WFOE is found to be a shell or a conduit without commercial substance, the tax authority may recharacterize income, disallow deductions for intercompany payments, impose a special tax adjustment, impose interest at the benchmark lending rate plus 5 percentage points, and potentially attribute undistributed profits of the company to the ultimate shareholding party. All intercompany arrangements must be documented with contracts, invoices, board minutes, and evidence of actual personnel and functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through False Accounting and Concealment of Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating revenue, manipulating Apple IAP and Paymentwall settlement reports, creating fictitious expenses, using duplicate invoices, or maintaining off-book bank accounts to reduce the corporate income tax liability of the WFOE. The act includes directing the accountant to fabricate financial statements or intentionally misreporting Box 1 revenue in the annual tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under PRC Tax Collection Administration Law (TCAL) Article 63, the taxpayer shall be ordered to pay the overdue tax within a time limit, with a penalty of 50% to 500% of the unpaid tax. If the amount evaded is sufficiently large and constitutes a crime, Criminal Law Article 201 applies: evasion of more than 10% of taxable income and exceeding RMB 100,000 can lead to imprisonment of up to 3 years or criminal detention, plus fines; evasion exceeding 30% of taxable income and over RMB 300,000 can lead to imprisonment of 3-7 years plus fines. The enterprise will also be listed in the Major Tax Violation Case List, leading to joint punishment, restriction on VAT invoicing, credit downgrade, and revocation of relevant licenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may pierce the corporate veil where the WFOE is proven to be a mere instrumentality of the directors. Directors who initiate or approve the fraudulent scheme are personally and jointly liable for civil restitution of unpaid taxes, interest, penalties and the company's losses. Under Criminal Law, the responsible director faces personal fines, imprisonment of up to 7 years, confiscation of illicit gains, and a travel ban (blacklisting) that prohibits exit from China. Additionally, the director may be disqualified from serving as a director or senior manager in any enterprise for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Remit Withholding Tax on Outbound Dividends, Interest, and Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to the Taiwan shareholder without deducting the 10% withholding tax, or paying interest and royalties to a non-resident without withholding income tax. Also includes disguising dividends as loan repayments, excessive management fees, or transfer pricing adjustments to circumvent the WHT obligation. The WFOE, as the statutory withholding agent, fails to file the withholding return and remit the tax within the statutory 7-day window after payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under TCAL Article 69, a withholding agent that fails to withhold and remit the tax is subject to a fine of 50% to 300% of the un-withheld tax. The tax authority will also order the agent to recover the tax from the non-resident or, if impossible, may assess the tax against the agent. In addition, TCAL Article 32 imposes a daily late payment surcharge of 0.05% of the overdue WHT from the due date. If the withholding failure is intentional and committed to evade tax, the responsible person may face criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Article 201, with imprisonment up to 7 years for severe cases. The WFOE's name will be published as a serious tax violation, and its export invoice quota may be restricted.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the finance officer who knowingly design a structure to avoid dividend WHT, or who fail to implement the withholding system, are personally liable for the penalty imposed on the company. The corporate veil may be pierced if the dividend distribution is made in a way that depletes corporate assets while the shareholder is the controlling director, allowing creditors and tax authorities to recover against the director's personal assets. Directors face civil liability for the unpaid withholding and fines, a travel ban (exit restriction), and in criminal cases imprisonment of 3-7 years and fines. The director's personal bank accounts and property may be frozen and seized under asset preservation measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Shell Company Abuse Preventing Arm's Length Taxation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE enters into cross-border arrangements with the Taiwan parent that set transfer prices for services, royalties, or interest at levels that artificially shift profits out of China, such as paying excessive royalties for barely used IP, allocating debt at non-arm's length interest, or receiving no compensation for services it actually performs. The company does not prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation despite exceeding statutory thresholds, and its office lacks real employees and operational substance, serving only as a pass-through for the Taiwan parent's video-app activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under EIT Law Article 41, the tax authority may re-determine taxable income using an arm's length method; Article 48 imposes interest on the adjusted underpayment at the benchmark central bank rate plus 5 percentage points. Under Article 44, if the taxpayer fails to provide relevant materials, the tax authority may assess income based on the information available. False transfer pricing documentation may be treated as tax evasion under TCAL Article 63, triggering a penalty of 50%-500% of the underpaid tax. Under GAAR (Article 47), the authority can recharacterize the whole structure and deny the deduction of all related-party payments. Additionally, the CFC rules (Article 45) can attribute undistributed profits of the offshore entity to the WFOE if the entity is not considered to have sufficient economic substance. The failure to provide Local File on request incurs a fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 under TCAL Article 62.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or implement artificial transfer pricing structures without commercial justification are personally liable for the tax adjustment, interest and penalties if the corporate form is abused. PRC Company Law Article 20 permits piercing the veil where corporate personality is used to avoid taxes, allowing personal assets to be seized. Directors and controlling shareholders are jointly and severally liable for the full amount of the additional tax plus interest and penalties. Criminal liability can arise if the TP misstatement is found to be fraudulent evasion: imprisonment of up to 7 years, fines, and disqualification from serving as directors. A travel ban is routinely imposed in major tax evasion cases, and the director's assets may be transferred or confiscated to satisfy the tax debt.
